reasoning_content:
The bash /dev/tcp WS handshake returned empty output. Let me retry with a different approach — I could also do the HTTP upgrade via `curl`, or check the hocuspocus logs for connection attempts. Actually, Hocuspocus provides an HTTP endpoint at the same port (according to the logs, HTTP: http://0.0.0.0:1234). Let me hit it with curl to check for a response, and try the WS handshake again with a longer read.

The reason the handshake test returned empty might be that the server is waiting… no, actually Hocuspocus (which uses ws) responds to the upgrade request. The bash approach using `head -c 200` and `exec 3<&-` might have an issue: `timeout 5 head -c 200 <&3` — this should work. But nothing was output. Maybe the connection got reset. Let me retry with an explicit read loop, or test with curl.

Let me also verify that the hocuspocus server is responding on the HTTP side. Hocuspocus v2 has an HTTP server (it can be used for health checks). Let me try `curl http://localhost:1234/`.

action.command:
cd /tmp && cat > wstest.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/1234 || { echo "CONNECT FAIL"; exit 1; }
printf 'GET /board/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost:1234\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n' >&3
sleep 2
head -c 400 <&3
exec 3>&- 3<&-
EOF
chmod +x wstest.sh && ./wstest.sh; echo; echo "=== HTTP probe ==="; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' --max-time 5 http://localhost:1234/ ; curl -sS --max-time 5 http://localhost:1234/ | head -c 200; echo
